chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who prayed without purity, or forgot a prayer that he did not perform, or slept through it, so he said:

He should make up the missed prayer whenever he remembers it, whether he remembers it at night or during the day. When the time for the current prayer enters and he has not yet completed the missed one, he should proceed with the current prayer that has arrived, as it is more entitled to its time, so he should pray it. After he has made it up, he should pray the missed one that has passed, and he should not offer a voluntary (nafl) rak'ah until he has completed all the obligatory (fard) prayers.

key_terms.يَقْضِيهَا: He makes it up / performs the missed prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for making up a missed prayer if the time for the next prayer has already arrived?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural priority between current and missed obligatory prayers, establishing that if the time for a new prayer enters while a previous one remains unperformed, the current prayer takes precedence to ensure it is not missed. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the sanctity of prayer times while ensuring the fulfillment of all duties, distinguishing between the urgency of the current time and the catch-up of past obligations. It further reinforces the principle that voluntary (nafl) prayers should not be performed until all obligatory (fard) prayers are completed, reflecting a structured approach to worship.
